To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the weak well posedness of the strongly damed linear wave equation and the non linear Westervalte equation with homogeneous Diriclet boundary conditions is proved on arbitrary three-dimensional domains or any two-dimensional domains which can be obtined by a limit of NT domains caracterized by the same geometric constants.

the solutions of the Westerveld equation on an arbitrary domains in \mathbf{R}^d$ can be approximated by solutions on a sequence of domains which are either NTA domains in d=2$ or Sobolev extension domain in $d\le 3$ with a $C^d$ boundary.

the weak well posedness of the strongly dampled linear wave equation and the Westervelt non linear wave equation with homogeneous Dirchlet boundary condition can be proved on a wide class of domains including the class of admissable domains and on arbitrary domains in \mathbf{R}^d$, 3\le d\le 3$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the well posedness and the asymptotic behavior of the solution of the wave equation with Dirichlet boundary value on arbitrary domains.
the study of the well-posedness of the strongly dampled linear and the non linear wave equations with Dirichlet boundary value on arbitrary domains in \mathfrak{R}^N$.
the well-posedness of linear and nonlinear wave problems on fractal domains, and the convergence of the solutions of these problems on fractal and smooth domains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have obtained the weak well posedness for the Westerveld equation on any domain in \mathbb {R}^3$, any domain in \mbox{ \mathbb{ R}}^2$ which can be obtained as a limit of NTD domains with the same geometrical characteristics and for any domain which can be obtained from a domain with Lipschitz boundary by removing an arbitrary finite number of balls.
we have obtained the existence and uniqueness of solutions for the linear damped and the nonlinear Westervelt wave equation on a wide class of domains.
the Westervelt model is well posed in a wide range of domains and boundary conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the weak well-posedness of the linear and nonlinear wave equation on arbitrary domains is equivalent to the weak well- posedness of the linear equation with the Dirichlet boundary on the class of admissable domains.
the weak solutions of the Westerveld equation with homogeneous or non homogeneous Dirichle boundary conditions can be obtained on arbitrary domains in \math{R}^d$ for any d\ge 1$

the well posedness of the Dirichlet problem for the Westervel equation is proved on any bounded domain with a $d-1$ boundary $d \ge 2$ which is an admissible domain in the class defined by the Markov's local inequalities.

it is possible to obtain the well posedness results for the linear and the nonlinear wave equation on domains with fractal boundary.
